# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (empty seed)
- Strategy tried: multi-class batch in one candidate — code enforcement for the
  deterministic clusters (payment format/amount, payment_history re-sync, baggage
  recompute, enriched COMMUNICATE returns, actionable errors) + explicit mid-model
  prose for the behavioral clusters (anti-stall, speak-the-figure, act-vs-transfer).
  Diagnosed with a single Explore subagent over all 30 trajectories, then verified
  every code edit on the LIVE airline DB (payment splits, refund = $5244, baggage
  no-op) before shipping. Gate result not yet known (LEDGER will stamp it).
- Plateau/stall signal: none yet (iteration 1).
- What to try next iteration: read the RESULT. The stall/USER_STOP cluster (A) is the
  biggest and is only prose-mitigated — if it dominates residual loss, the next lever
  is structural (same-turn execute, user-sim-driven) not another prose rule. For the
  wrong-reservation cluster (D) an untried design is a route→reservation resolver tool.
  Avoid re-touching the verified-no-op code paths (auto-correct/recompute) — broadening
  them into always-on rewrites is the regression risk.

## Iteration cand_0002
- Strategy tried: diagnosed the dominant residual loss by comparing FAILING vs PASSING
  turn-endings on the SAME tasks (not just reading failures). Finding: the killer is a
  `###STOP###`-terminal confirm stall — the agent ends a turn on "Shall I proceed?",
  the user says "yes###STOP###", and the episode ends before any write. Lever mix this
  iteration: a prose decision-chain rewrite for the behavioral stall (A), a knowledge
  rule for a wrong refusal (B), tightened transfer/finish rules (C), and a code
  composite `modify_reservation` for multi-write tasks (D). Four edit TYPES, not one.
- Key process insight: for a behavioral cluster, READ the passing trials of the same
  task — they tell you the exact winning micro-behavior to codify (here: execute the
  write directly, no separate confirm turn). This is stronger than reasoning from the
  failures alone.
- Plateau/stall signal: none yet (parent was an accept; all tasks unresolved <2·SE).
- What to try next iteration: read cand_0002's RESULT. If the stall (A) persists, the
  only remaining lever is structural — remove the update_* primitives so
  `modify_reservation` (one decisive call) is the only modify path; weigh against the
  regression risk on passing 11/37/40. If A moved but booking tasks (8/23/25) remain,
  shift to the certificate/multi-card payment-split path in book_reservation.

<!-- cap-evolve:meta-insights-append-below -->

## Iteration cand_0003 (last iteration of this run)
- Strategy tried, and whether it moved val: the dominant stall from cand_0001/0002 is
  fixed, so I re-diagnosed from THIS iteration's val trajectories rather than inheriting
  the old cluster map, and found the residual loss is three decision/behavioral clusters
  (A dup/compounding write, B wrong write-action, C grab-first-reservation). Shipped a
  deliberate CODE+PROSE mix: new `find_reservation` resolver tool + `book_reservation`
  dup-guard (code) and RULES 6/7 + cancel-eligibility checklist (prose), 6 edits across
  both surfaces. Gate result not yet known (LEDGER will stamp it) — this is the final
  planned iteration so there is no next one to read it.
- Key process insight reconfirmed: once a dominant cluster is fixed, STOP trusting the
  previous iteration's diagnosis — re-cluster from the current champion's own
  trajectories. The failure mix shifts under you; cand_0002's "stall" map would have
  wasted this iteration. Also: the grab-first-id finding (17/22 touch the WRONG
  reservation, not an omitted field) was ONLY visible by diffing failing-vs-passing
  tool-call TARGETS on the same task — the summary's "omitted cabin upgrade" read was
  wrong. Always verify the actual tool arguments against the live DB before diagnosing.
- Plateau/stall signal and lever switched to: NOT flat — two straight accepts (+0.133,
  +0.100). To pre-empt a prose-only plateau on the mid (~100B) reader, I added code
  levers (resolver + guard) this iteration rather than a third round of prose rules.
  The behavioral clusters that remain (B especially, the adversarial cancel+split in 23)
  are the ones prose alone is weakest at — code guards are the lever with headroom.
- What to try next iteration (if a cand_0004 happens): read cand_0003's RESULT. If C
  (17/22) moved, the resolver works — keep it and consider making route-matching the
  default inside the write tools. If B (23/11/19) still loses, the untried code lever is
  a discriminating guard (cancel-eligibility `reason` parameter; session anti-split in
  `book_reservation`). If A (12) persists, revisit idempotent modify only with a minimal,
  fully live-DB-verified snapshot-restore. If cand_0003 is REJECTED, its diff.patch isol-
  ates the culprit — most likely E2 (dup-guard) blocking a legitimate corrective re-book;
  the fallback is to keep E1/E3/E4/E5/E6 and drop E2.
